sentences.zh: 罗马人从共和国转变为帝国。

sentences.zh: 都铎王朝将修道院改造成了乡村别墅。

sentences.en: From waste to efficiency.

sentences.en: From dependence to control.

sentences.en: From consumption to contribution.

sentences.en: So history's next great transformation may not be happening in parliaments or palaces.
sentences.zh: 所以，历史上下一个伟大的变革可能不会发生在议会或宫殿里。

sentences.en: When Nelson's carriage drew up outside Neret's hotel in one of central London's most elegant streets,
sentences.zh: 当纳尔逊的马车停在伦敦市中心一条最优雅街道上的内雷特酒店外时，

sentences.en: the pavement was packed with well-wishers.
sentences.zh: 人行道上挤满了祝福的人群。

sentences.en: He was dressed in full uniform with three stars on his breast and two gold medals, reported the Naval Chronicle, and was welcomed by repeated huzzahs from the crowd,
sentences.zh: 据《海军纪事》报道，他身着全套制服，胸前佩戴着三颗星和两枚金质奖章，受到了人群阵阵欢呼的欢迎，

sentences.en: which he returned with a low bow.
sentences.zh: 他以深鞠躬回礼。

sentences.en: He looked extremely well, but in person very thin.
sentences.zh: 他看起来气色极好，但本人却非常消瘦。

sentences.en: In the hotel lobby, Fanny and Edmund were waiting, nervously wringing their hands.
sentences.zh: 在酒店大堂里，范妮和埃德蒙正紧张地绞着双手等待着。

sentences.en: When they saw him, relief and joy flashed across their faces.
sentences.zh: 当他们看到他时，脸上闪过一丝宽慰和喜悦。

sentences.en: Then, two more figures came in behind him.
sentences.zh: 接着，他身后又走进来两个人。

sentences.en: An older man long-faced and beaky-nosed.
sentences.zh: 一位长脸鹰钩鼻的老年男子。

sentences.en: And a younger woman, with an enormous mass of chestnut hair.
sentences.zh: 还有一位有着一头浓密栗色长发的年轻女子。

sentences.en: And almost bursting out of her dress.
sentences.zh: 而且她的身材几乎要撑破了裙子。

sentences.en: And although Fanny tried to smile, it was as if somebody had snuffed out all the lights.
sentences.zh: 尽管范妮试图微笑，但感觉就像有人熄灭了所有的灯光一样。

sentences.en: So that, of course, is from Adventures in Time, Nelson, Hero of the Seas, by our very own Dominic Sandbrook, out in paperback today.
sentences.zh: 所以，这段内容当然出自我们自己的多米尼克·桑德布鲁克所著的《时间冒险：海上的英雄纳尔逊》，今天平装版已经上市了。

sentences.en: And it gives you a sense of the incredible stylistic range of this book.
sentences.zh: 它让你感受到了这本书令人难以置信的文体跨度。

sentences.en: In the previous one, we had some vivid and highly original travel writing.
sentences.zh: 在上一本书中，我们读到了一些生动且极具原创性的游记。

sentences.en: Naples is a city of contrasts.
sentences.zh: 那不勒斯是一座充满对比的城市。

sentences.en: And now, with this scene, we are launched into something redolent of, well, of kind of, some sites might say melodrama,
sentences.zh: 而现在，通过这个场景，我们进入了一种让人联想到——嗯，怎么说呢，有些地方可能会说是情节剧，

sentences.en: others, more kindly, might say reminiscent of Jane Austen, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 而其他人，比较客气的话，可能会说让人想起简·奥斯汀的作品。

sentences.en: So the scene, it's on the 8th of November, 1800.
sentences.zh: 这个场景发生在 1800 年 11 月 8 日。

sentences.en: Nelson has been away for more than two years from his wife, Fanny, and his father, the vicar.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊已经离开他的妻子范妮和他的父亲——那位牧师埃德蒙·纳尔逊——两年多了。

sentences.en: Edmund Nelson.
sentences.zh: 埃德蒙·纳尔逊。

sentences.en: And they realise, to their horror, that he has brought with him, to their meeting,
sentences.zh: 他们惊恐地意识到，他在这次会面中竟然带来了

sentences.en: his mistress, Emma Hamilton, who is pregnant by Nelson.
sentences.zh: 他的情妇艾玛·汉密尔顿，而且她还怀着纳尔逊的孩子。

sentences.en: So hence Dominic's very diplomatic description of her bursting out of her dress.
sentences.zh: 所以多米尼克才用了那种非常外交辞令的描述，说她“几乎要撑破了裙子”。

sentences.en: And her husband, Sir William.
sentences.zh: 还有她的丈夫，威廉爵士。

sentences.en: Her elderly husband, Sir William.
sentences.zh: 她年迈的丈夫，威廉爵士。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is either the rankest melodrama, or reminiscent of Mansfield Park.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这要么是极其庸俗的情节剧，要么让人想起《曼斯菲尔德庄园》。

sentences.en: Take your pick.
sentences.zh: 随你怎么选。

sentences.en: But it's high, high drama, isn't it, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 但这确实是极具戏剧性的，不是吗，多米尼克？

sentences.en: It is indeed, Tom.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，汤姆。

sentences.en: We should be getting into more soap opera-style shenanigans later in this episode.
sentences.zh: 本集稍后我们会深入探讨更多肥皂剧式的闹剧。

sentences.en: But maybe first, we should remind ourselves where we've got to.
sentences.zh: 但也许我们应该先回顾一下我们讲到了哪里。

sentences.en: So, this is the first time Nelson has been in England since April 1798.
sentences.zh: 这是纳尔逊自 1798 年 4 月以来第一次回到英国。

sentences.en: Listeners will recall that he chased Napoleon's fleet across the Mediterranean, destroyed them at the Battle of the Nile,
sentences.zh: 听众们会记得，他曾在地中海追击拿破仑的舰队，并在尼罗河战役中摧毁了他们，

sentences.en: then went north to Naples and was embroiled in the poisonous politics of the kingdom of the two Sicilies.
sentences.zh: 随后北上那不勒斯，卷入了那不勒斯王国那充满毒性的政治斗争中。

sentences.en: And there he slightly let himself down, I think we agreed,
sentences.zh: 而且我们一致认为，他在那里稍微有点自毁形象，

sentences.en: by shooting.
sentences.zh: 因为他处决了俘虏。

sentences.en: Yeah, shooting prisoners that he said he wouldn't shoot.
sentences.zh: 没错，处决了他曾承诺不会处决的俘虏。

sentences.en: And then he started, or about the same time, he started an affair with the wife of the British minister in Naples, Emma Hamilton, who we met earlier on.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，他开始与那不勒斯的英国公使夫人艾玛·汉密尔顿发生婚外情，我们之前提到过她。

sentences.en: So, shall we pick up the story in the late summer of 1799?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们从 1799 年夏末继续讲起好吗？

sentences.en: Let's.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, this republic that was set up in Naples, the Parthenopian Republic, has been crushed.
sentences.zh: 在那不勒斯建立的那个共和国，即帕特诺佩共和国，已经被镇压了。

sentences.en: King Ferdinand and Oaf, Queen Maria Carolina, you ventriloquised her as Bill Sykes.
sentences.zh: 费迪南德国王和那个“笨蛋”玛丽亚·卡罗琳王后——你曾用比尔·赛克斯来形容她——

sentences.en: They are back on their thrones.
sentences.zh: 他们已经重回王位。

sentences.en: Nelson is the temporary commander-in-chief in the Mediterranean, but he's keeping the seat warm until casting agents' favourite Scotsman,
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊是地中海的临时总司令，但他只是在为选角导演最喜欢的苏格兰人——

sentences.en: when Admiral Lord Keith returns from leave.
sentences.zh: 基思海军上将休假归来前——暂代职位。

sentences.en: He is very much not a man who would look favourably on a former prostitute doing attitudes.
sentences.zh: 他绝对不是那种会欣赏一个前妓女搔首弄姿的人。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, the priority really is the Admiralty want to retake Malta, where there is a French garrison, because, of course, Napoleon took Malta on his way to Egypt.
sentences.zh: 所以，海军部的首要任务实际上是夺回马耳他，那里有法国驻军，因为拿破仑在去埃及的路上占领了马耳他。

sentences.en: And historians disagree about this, and indeed Nelson's own contemporaries disagreed about it, whether Nelson's heart was really in retaking Malta or whether he was distracted.
sentences.zh: 历史学家对此有分歧，事实上纳尔逊的同时代人对此也有分歧，即纳尔逊是否真的全心全意想夺回马耳他，还是他分心了。

sentences.en: I'm sure we will come to this later on.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们稍后会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: He has based himself not in Naples, but back in Palermo, where he is joined with the Hamiltons.
sentences.zh: 他没有把基地设在那不勒斯，而是回到了巴勒莫，在那里他与汉密尔顿夫妇会合了。

sentences.en: And again, there are criticisms at the time, aren't there, that he has perhaps lost sight of his duty,
sentences.zh: 当时也有批评声音，不是吗？说他可能忘记了自己的职责，

sentences.en: and that he prefers to moon around with Emma in Palermo than going off and attacking Naples.
sentences.zh: 比起去进攻那不勒斯，他更喜欢在巴勒莫和艾玛厮混。

sentences.en: But, Tom, you think that's a little bit harsh?
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，你觉得这有点苛刻吗？

sentences.en: I do, because the pitch is that Nelson is Antony frolicking with Cleopatra in the fleshpots of Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是，因为人们总是把纳尔逊比作在亚历山大的温柔乡里与克利奥帕特拉调情的安东尼。

sentences.en: That's the parallel that people endlessly, endlessly draw.
sentences.zh: 这是人们不断、不断引用的类比。

sentences.en: But the thing is, Palermo is not at all a mad base from which to prosecute what Nelson, as acting commander-in-chief in the Mediterranean,
sentences.zh: 但问题是，对于纳尔逊作为地中海代理总司令所认为的职责来说，巴勒莫根本不是一个疯狂的基地，

sentences.en: sees as his responsibilities, which are chiefly to keep an eye on the endangered Kingdom of Naples, and if possible, to roll the French backwards up through Italy.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己的职责主要是关注岌岌可危的那不勒斯王国，如果可能的话，将法国人从意大利赶出去。

sentences.en: And secondly, to maintain and coordinate the blockade of Malta, because the fall of Malta will give Britain an absolute strategic naval prize.
sentences.zh: 其次，是维持和协调对马耳他的封锁，因为马耳他的陷落将给英国带来绝对的战略海军奖赏。

sentences.en: And the thing is that, although Britain is funding some of the blockade, the other key person who is contributing towards this blockade is Ferdinand.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，虽然英国资助了部分封锁，但另一个为封锁做出贡献的关键人物是费迪南德。

sentences.en: And the reason he's doing that is because he basically thinks that he's going to end up with Malta.
sentences.zh: 他之所以这样做，是因为他基本上认为自己最终会得到马耳他。

sentences.en: I mean, whether he does, we will see.
sentences.zh: 至于他是否能如愿，我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: But I think that there are lots of people who don't understand what Nelson is facing at this time, the threads that he's holding in his hand.
sentences.zh: 但我认为很多人并不了解纳尔逊当时所面临的局面，以及他手中所掌控的错综复杂的局势。

sentences.en: And so they assume, well, the only reason he could possibly have for lying in Palermo is because he's...
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为，他留在巴勒莫的唯一理由就是因为他……

sentences.en: Canoodling is the word.
sentences.zh: “卿卿我我”是这个词。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, I mean, both of those things can be true at once, can't they?
sentences.zh: 但是，这两件事可以同时成立，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it's possible that there were good grounds to be in Palermo, and yet at the same time there's undoubtedly an awful lot of canoodling.
sentences.zh: 因为留在巴勒莫可能有正当理由，但与此同时，毫无疑问也有大量的卿卿我我。

sentences.en: Even Nelson's, probably one of his most admired biographers, John Sugden, has this stuff he describes as a repugnant cell of self-congratulation, flattery,
sentences.zh: 即使是纳尔逊最受推崇的传记作者之一约翰·萨格登，也描述了巴勒莫宫廷中那种令人反感的自我吹捧、阿谀奉承和操纵行为，

sentences.en: and manipulation in the court in Palermo.
sentences.zh: 他称之为一种令人作呕的氛围。

sentences.en: And he talks about the sort of intoxicating sultriness about the Palazzo Palagonia, fatally attractive, like a delicious sin.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了帕拉戈尼亚宫那种令人陶醉的闷热感，致命地吸引人，就像一种美味的罪恶。

sentences.en: Now, a lot of this, you could say, is artistic projection, and a lot of this is describing the court rather than Nelson himself.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以说这其中很多是艺术化的投射，而且很多是在描述宫廷，而不是纳尔逊本人。

sentences.en: But there is a sense at the time, among some of Nelson's comrades, that he has succumbed to the allure.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，纳尔逊的一些战友确实有一种感觉，认为他屈服于这种诱惑了。

sentences.en: And this is the only time in his career when people make that claim, right?
sentences.zh: 这是他职业生涯中唯一一次人们提出这种说法，对吧？

sentences.en: They never make it at any other point.
sentences.zh: 他们在其他任何时候都没有这样说过。

sentences.en: That he's succumbed to the allure, the exoticism, and the sensuality, and all of this.
sentences.zh: 说他屈服于这种诱惑、异国情调、感官享受等等。

sentences.en: I think that this is a tradition that goes back, obviously people are saying this at the time, it feeds into biographies of Nelson throughout the 19th and 20th century,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种传统，显然人们在当时就这么说，这影响了整个 19 和 20 世纪的纳尔逊传记，

sentences.en: who are generally written by kind of bluff naval types.
sentences.zh: 这些传记通常是由那种直率的海军军官写的。

sentences.en: And I just don't think that they approve of Italians, of showgirls.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得他们不赞成意大利人，不赞成那些交际花。

sentences.en: I think there's a kind of weird obsession with the idea that everything Nelson is doing is because he's been seduced by A, Emma Hamilton,
sentences.zh: 我认为有一种奇怪的执念，认为纳尔逊所做的一切都是因为他被 A，艾玛·汉密尔顿，

sentences.en: and B, the fleshpots of Italy, Palermo, Naples, take your pick.
sentences.zh: 和 B，意大利、巴勒莫、那不勒斯的温柔乡所诱惑，随你怎么选。

sentences.en: And the two get elided.
sentences.zh: 这两者被混为一谈了。

sentences.en: You know, I think undoubtedly he is having this affair, probably hasn't gone beyond the canoodling stage by this point.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为毫无疑问他在进行这段婚外情，到目前为止可能还没超过卿卿我我的阶段。

sentences.en: But I think equally, he can have this affair, but it doesn't stop him from being as effective and efficient and dynamic as he has ever been.
sentences.zh: 但我同样认为，他可以进行这段婚外情，但这并不妨碍他像以往一样高效、有效和充满活力。

sentences.en: And yet there are complaints from very early on, from people who have gone to visit him, people who might be expected to be sympathetic to him,
sentences.zh: 然而，很早就有人抱怨，那些去拜访他的人，那些本应同情他的人，

sentences.en: who feel that something has gone wrong.
sentences.zh: 觉得出了什么问题。

sentences.en: I'll just give you a couple of examples.
sentences.zh: 我给你举几个例子。

sentences.en: So one of them is Lord and Lady Elgin.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是埃尔金伯爵和伯爵夫人。

sentences.en: Lord and Lady Elgin are going through Palermo on their way to Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 埃尔金伯爵夫妇在前往君士坦丁堡的途中经过巴勒莫。

sentences.en: Lady Elgin writes of Nelson and the Hamiltons, and their relationship with the royal family.
sentences.zh: 埃尔金夫人写到了纳尔逊和汉密尔顿夫妇，以及他们与王室的关系。

sentences.en: I never saw three people made such thorough dupes of as Lady Hamilton, Sir William, and Lord Nelson.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过像汉密尔顿夫人、威廉爵士和纳尔逊勋爵这样被彻底愚弄的三个人。

sentences.en: It's really humiliating to see Lord Nelson as if he had no other thought than her.
sentences.zh: 看到纳尔逊勋爵好像除了她之外什么都不想，真是太丢人了。

sentences.en: This is actually Maria Carolina.
sentences.zh: 这其实是玛丽亚·卡罗琳说的。

sentences.en: Is it not a pity that a man who had gained so much credit should fling himself away in this shameful manner?
sentences.zh: 一个赢得了如此多声誉的人，竟然以这种可耻的方式自毁前程，难道不可惜吗？

sentences.en: Now, that's not an uncommon thing to say.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么罕见的说法。

sentences.en: So the other example I was going to give you was Nelson's old friend, Thomas Trubridge, with whom he later falls out.
sentences.zh: 我要举的另一个例子是纳尔逊的老朋友托马斯·特鲁布里奇，后来他们闹翻了。

sentences.en: Trubridge wrote to him and said,
sentences.zh: 特鲁布里奇写信给他说：

sentences.en: Please, I'm hearing really disturbing reports about you.
sentences.zh: 拜托，我听到了关于你非常令人不安的报道。

sentences.en: If you knew what your friends feel for you, I'm sure you would cut out all the nocturnal parties.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道你的朋友们为你感到多么难过，我相信你会取消所有的夜间派对。

sentences.en: The gambling of the people in Palermo is publicly talked about everywhere.
sentences.zh: 巴勒莫人们的赌博行为到处都在公开议论。

sentences.en: I beseech your lordship, leave off.
sentences.zh: 我恳求阁下，停止吧。

sentences.en: Lady Hamilton's character will suffer.
sentences.zh: 汉密尔顿夫人的名声会受损的。

sentences.en: Nothing can prevent people from talking.
sentences.zh: 没有什么能阻止人们议论。

sentences.en: A gambling woman in the eye of an Englishman is loSt.
sentences.zh: 在英国人眼中，一个好赌的女人就完了。

sentences.en: Now, putting that last bit on one side, this sort of sense that is clearly current, not just among later Victorian biographies or whatever, but among some of Nelson's friends,
sentences.zh: 撇开最后一点不谈，这种感觉显然很普遍，不仅是在后来的维多利亚时代传记中，而且在纳尔逊的一些朋友中也是如此，

sentences.en: that his focus isn't quite what it was, that he's keeping late hours, that maybe you can say some of this is projection and some of this is Antony and Cleopatra,
sentences.zh: 认为他的注意力不如以前了，他熬夜太晚，也许你可以说其中一些是投射，一些是安东尼和克利奥帕特拉的故事，

sentences.en: but surely not all of it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但肯定不全是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: No, I mean, clearly it causes gossip, it causes scandal.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，这显然引起了流言蜚语，引起了丑闻。

sentences.en: The two most, you know, the most famous man, the most famous woman in Britain having an affair.
sentences.zh: 英国最著名的男人和最著名的女人发生了婚外情。

sentences.en: I mean, of course, I mean, it's absolute catnip for anyone who loves a scandal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，这对任何喜欢丑闻的人来说绝对是诱饵。

sentences.en: And bear in mind that that thing you read about, you know, it's shameful what's going on here.
sentences.zh: 记住你读到的那件事，你知道，这里发生的事情是可耻的。

sentences.en: This is about Nelson's relationship to the Queen of Naples.
sentences.zh: 这是关于纳尔逊与那不勒斯王后的关系。

sentences.en: And I think that the feeling is that a British admiral should not be behaving like a flunky to rulers of some kind of tin pot Italian kingdom.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们的感觉是，英国海军上将不应该表现得像某个三流意大利王国的统治者的跟班。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's that's the vibe, basically.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这基本上就是那种氛围。

sentences.en: And you could argue that perhaps Nelson is clinging to them too closely.
sentences.zh: 你可以争辩说，也许纳尔逊与他们走得太近了。

sentences.en: But bear in mind, those are the orders he's been given.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，那是他接到的命令。

sentences.en: He has been told, you know, look after them carefully.
sentences.zh: 他被告知，你知道，要小心照顾他们。

sentences.en: And I think you can absolutely make the case in terms of military strategy that maintaining the integrity of Britain's only real ally of significance in the Mediterranean at a time when Nelson is responsible for establishing the supremacy of the Royal Navy in the face of French threats.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，从军事战略的角度来看，在纳尔逊负责在法国威胁面前确立皇家海军霸权的时期，维持英国在地中海唯一重要的真正盟友的完整性，绝对是可以论证的。

sentences.en: I think that is a reasonable strategic position to take.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个合理的战略立场。

sentences.en: Now, when Keith arrives, you know, he's very disapproving of Nelson's relationship with Emma Hamilton for, you know, I mean, of course, I mean,
sentences.zh: 现在，当基思到达时，你知道，他非常不赞成纳尔逊与艾玛·汉密尔顿的关系，你知道，我的意思是，当然，

sentences.en: that's that's his kind of moral position.
sentences.zh: 那是他那种道德立场。

sentences.en: But I think the much more deep seated reason for the disagreements between the two men is that Keith isn't as convinced as Nelson is that the Italian theatre is important.
sentences.zh: 但我认为两人之间分歧更深层的原因是，基思不像纳尔逊那样确信意大利战区很重要。

sentences.en: His focus is much more on Manioka, on Spain, on Gibraltar.
sentences.zh: 他的重心更多是在马尼奥卡、西班牙和直布罗陀。

sentences.en: And that is a strategic disagreement.
sentences.zh: 这是一个战略分歧。

sentences.en: And the fact that Keith is coming to replace Nelson and that Keith is is not good at handling Nelson, you know, he's not afraid to insult him, to be rude to him,
sentences.zh: 事实上，基思来接替纳尔逊，而且基思不擅长处理与纳尔逊的关系，你知道，他不怕侮辱他，对他粗鲁，

sentences.en: to inflict what Nelson sees as snubs only adds to the mix.
sentences.zh: 对他施加纳尔逊所认为的冷遇，只会让情况变得更复杂。

sentences.en: And I think that Keith's criticism of Nelson for having a relationship with Lady Hamilton and the more general gossip is veiling deeper seated disagreements between Nelson and his peers and immediate superiors in the Navy about the course,
sentences.zh: 我认为基思对纳尔逊与汉密尔顿夫人保持关系的批评，以及更广泛的流言蜚语，其实掩盖了纳尔逊与他在海军中的同僚及直属上级之间在战略方针上更深层次的分歧，

sentences.en: basically, of strategy.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，是关于战略的问题。

sentences.en: Well, there are a number of different things here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其中涉及很多不同的因素。

sentences.en: So one of them, amid the general swirl, is that there's a backlash more generally against the Hamiltons.
sentences.zh: 其中之一，在普遍的舆论漩涡中，是对汉密尔顿夫妇更广泛的抵制。

sentences.en: And that includes Sir William as well as Emma.
sentences.zh: 这不仅包括艾玛，也包括威廉爵士。

sentences.en: So Sir William Hamilton, there is definitely a sense after the failure of the Neapolitan expedition to Rome and then the huge fiasco of the revolution and the recapture of Naples,
sentences.zh: 对于威廉·汉密尔顿爵士来说，在那不勒斯远征罗马失败，以及随后革命和那不勒斯被夺回的巨大惨败之后，人们确实有一种感觉，

sentences.en: there is definitely a sense, I think, that Sir William has become much too close to the royal family and that he's slightly lost the plot.
sentences.zh: 我认为，人们确实觉得威廉爵士与王室走得太近了，而且他有点失去了理智。

sentences.en: So he is replaced as ambassador effectively at the beginning of 1800 and a new ambassador is sent out to replace him.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在1800年初实际上被解除了大使职务，并派了一位新大使来接替他。

sentences.en: And when he gets back to England, a big theme will be he doesn't get the pension he expects and he doesn't get the peerage he expects.
sentences.zh: 当他回到英国时，一个主要的话题将是他没有得到预期的养老金，也没有得到预期的爵位。

sentences.en: And there's a sense in which people are like, well, the Hamiltons are useless.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，觉得汉密尔顿夫妇毫无用处。

sentences.en: I mean, I hear what you're saying, but from Lord Keith's perspective, he would say, I have this subordinate who is behaving like a diva, who does not follow my orders,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我明白你的意思，但从基思勋爵的角度来看，他会说，我有这样一个下属，表现得像个大牌明星，不听从我的命令，

sentences.en: who now thinks himself above the chain of command, the code of behavior that governs the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 他现在认为自己凌驾于指挥链之上，凌驾于管理皇家海军的行为准则之上。

sentences.en: Because, yes, he's a great star and all the rest of it, but he is sometimes flagrantly disobeying my orders when I tell him, go here.
sentences.zh: 因为，没错，他是一位伟大的明星，诸如此类，但当我命令他去某地时，他有时会公然违抗我的命令。

sentences.en: Nelson has always done that.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊一直都是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, that's his modus operandi.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是他的行事风格。

sentences.en: That's fine, but that's very annoying if you're a commanding officer.
sentences.zh: 这没问题，但如果你是指挥官，这会非常令人恼火。

sentences.en: Of course it is.
sentences.zh: 当然是这样。

sentences.en: But I think Keith's style of leadership is completely antithetical to the Nelson touch.
sentences.zh: 但我认为基思的领导风格与“纳尔逊风格”完全背道而驰。

sentences.en: He doesn't have room for it.
sentences.zh: 他没有容纳这种风格的空间。

sentences.en: And so they're constantly rubbing up against each other.
sentences.zh: 所以他们总是发生摩擦。

sentences.en: Nelson is also, I mean, Nelson is not, he's not brilliant at his own PR, is he?
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊也是，我的意思是，纳尔逊并不擅长处理自己的公关，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's begging Keith the whole time to let him go home.
sentences.zh: 因为他一直在乞求基思让他回家。

sentences.en: So it's not surprising that Keith thinks this guy is not fully committed.
sentences.zh: 所以基思认为这家伙心思不在工作上也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Nelson's constantly complaining about his health, about his mental health.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊一直在抱怨他的健康状况，他的心理健康状况。

sentences.en: He says he's got a pain, I've got a pain in my heart, all of this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他说他感到痛苦，我的心在痛，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: And Keith looks at him and don't forget, Keith has heard a lot of the rumors.
sentences.zh: 基思看着他，别忘了，基思听到了很多传闻。

sentences.en: So before Keith even arrived in January 1800, another admiral wrote to him and said, you know, watch out for this infatuation that Nelson has with Emma Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 所以早在基思于1800年1月到达之前，另一位海军上将就写信给他，说，你知道，要小心纳尔逊对艾玛·汉密尔顿的迷恋。

sentences.en: I think it's very sad that Nelson should have so sadly exposed himself to ridicule and censure.
sentences.zh: 我认为纳尔逊如此悲哀地让自己暴露在嘲笑和谴责之下，真是令人难过。

sentences.en: Now you could say, well, you know, this is just sort of moral puritanism and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以说，好吧，你知道，这只是一种道德上的清教主义之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then Keith then arrives in Palermo and says, I found it a scene of fulsome vanity and absurdity.
sentences.zh: 然后基思到达巴勒莫后说，我发现这里充满了虚伪的虚荣和荒谬。

sentences.en: And I know what you'll say, this is Keith kind of cosplaying a critic in Antony and Cleopatra or something, but that doesn't mean there's not an element of truth in it.
sentences.zh: 我知道你会怎么说，这有点像基思在扮演《安东尼与克莉奥佩特拉》里的评论家之类的角色，但这并不意味着其中没有事实成分。

sentences.en: No, I don't think he's doing that.
sentences.zh: 不，我不认为他在那样做。

sentences.en: I think he's trying to impose his authority, which is obviously what he should be doing because he's the commander in chief.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是在试图树立自己的权威，这显然是他应该做的，因为他是总司令。

sentences.en: But the problem is, is that Nelson, you know, Nelson wins victories by disobeying orders.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，纳尔逊，你知道，纳尔逊是通过违抗命令赢得胜利的。

sentences.en: That's also always been what he does.
sentences.zh: 这也是他一贯的做法。

sentences.en: So there's a classic example of this in the early months of 1800 and it relates to the blockade of Malta.
sentences.zh: 所以1800年初就有这方面的一个典型例子，它与马耳他封锁战有关。

sentences.en: So Keith orders Nelson to abandon Palermo and come to Menorca.
sentences.zh: 基思命令纳尔逊放弃巴勒莫，前往梅诺卡岛。

sentences.en: Nelson predictably ignores this.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，纳尔逊无视了这一命令。

sentences.en: He sails out and on the 18th of February, he wins the single most decisive engagement of the entire blockade of Malta, which is the key strategic objective for Britain.
sentences.zh: 他出海了，并在2月18日赢得了整个马耳他封锁战中最具决定性的一场交战，这是英国的关键战略目标。

sentences.en: He meets a French relief force headed by a ship, Les Generaux, which is one of the two ships that had escaped destruction at the Battle of the Nile.
sentences.zh: 他遇到了一支由“热内罗号”领头的法国救援部队，这是在尼罗河海战中逃脱毁灭的两艘船之一。

sentences.en: Well, Nelson captures it and he does this by ignoring Keith's orders and trusting to his own instincts, which is what he always does.
sentences.zh: 好吧，纳尔逊俘获了它，他通过无视基思的命令并相信自己的直觉做到了这一点，这正是他一贯的做法。

sentences.en: And I think you can see there exactly the tensions that have shadowed Nelson's entire career.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以从中清楚地看到那些一直笼罩着纳尔逊整个职业生涯的紧张关系。

sentences.en: Resentment that his commanding officers don't respect him.
sentences.zh: 因为他的指挥官不尊重他而产生的怨恨。

sentences.en: His commanding officers don't respect him because he's always prone to going off and doing his own thing.
sentences.zh: 他的指挥官不尊重他，因为他总是倾向于自行其是。

sentences.en: Then he goes and does his own thing and it turns out brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 然后他去做了他自己的事，结果却非常出色。

sentences.en: And this is a kind of an abiding theme.
sentences.zh: 这是一种持久的主题。

sentences.en: So he falls out, for instance, also with Sir John Jervis, his great patron, the Earl of St.
sentences.zh: 例如，他也与他的大恩人，圣文森特伯爵约翰·杰维斯爵士闹翻了，

sentences.en: Vincent, who likewise thinks he's insufferable.
sentences.zh: 后者同样认为他令人难以忍受。

sentences.en: Yeah, but that doesn't mean that they're all wrong and Nelson is always right.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这并不意味着他们都错了，而纳尔逊总是对的。

sentences.en: Lord Keith is trying to put the interests of the entire operation, the Royal Navy, firSt.
sentences.zh: 基思勋爵试图将整个行动，即皇家海军的利益放在首位。

sentences.en: John Sugden, who's the great Nelson biographer, I remember describing his books as the kind of war and peace of this gigantic epic.
sentences.zh: 约翰·萨格登，那位伟大的纳尔逊传记作者，我记得他曾将自己的书描述为这部宏大史诗的《战争与和平》。

sentences.en: I mean, he is really critical of Nelson in this point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他在这一点上对纳尔逊确实持批评态度。

sentences.en: For all Nelson's self-righteousness, he must have known he was disappointing members of his
sentences.zh: 尽管纳尔逊自以为是，但他一定知道自己让他的同行们感到失望，

sentences.en: profession, the brothers who had begged him to stay off Malta as well as his superiors in London.
sentences.zh: 那些曾恳求他留在马耳他之外的兄弟们，以及他在伦敦的上级。

sentences.en: He who had once been the fleet's greatest asset was now underperforming and becoming a hindrance to his commander-in-chief, a prima donna turning into a passenger.
sentences.zh: 他曾经是舰队最大的资产，现在却表现不佳，成了他总司令的累赘，一个正在变成乘客的歌剧女主角。

sentences.en: Nelson's heart was ruling his head, but for the first time in his life, he'd become an impediment rather than an asset to the service he'd loved.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊的情感战胜了理智，但他一生中第一次成为了他所热爱的军队的阻碍，而不是资产。

sentences.en: Now, Tom, I totally accept that you can take a contrary view of this.
sentences.zh: 现在，汤姆，我完全接受你可以对此持相反的观点。

sentences.en: Well, you can quote Sugden to a contrary view because he also says no one fought harder for Malta than Nelson.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以引用萨格登的相反观点，因为他也说没有人比纳尔逊为马耳他战斗得更努力了。

sentences.en: And that's clearly the case throughout this spell.
sentences.zh: 这在整个期间显然是事实。

sentences.en: But often he's disobeyed orders in doing so, which is...
sentences.zh: 但他在这样做时经常违抗命令，这……

sentences.en: There is an example of this shortly after he has seen off the French relief force and Keith
sentences.zh: 在他击退法国救援部队后不久，就有一个例子，基思

sentences.en: explicitly orders him, you know, don't go to Palermo, but Nelson does pleading ill health.
sentences.zh: 明确命令他，你知道，不要去巴勒莫，但纳尔逊以健康状况不佳为由还是去了。

sentences.en: Now, I think that that is probably genuine.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为这可能是真实的。

sentences.en: Nelson does seem to have been incredibly ill at this point.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊在这一点上似乎确实病得非常厉害。

sentences.en: To quote on this occasion, Andrew Lambert, another great biographer of Nelson, on the
sentences.zh: 引用纳尔逊的另一位伟大传记作者安德鲁·兰伯特的话，在

sentences.en: 18th of March, while on passage to Palermo, Nelson experienced chest pains that convinced him he was close to death.
sentences.zh: 3月18日，在前往巴勒莫的途中，纳尔逊经历了胸痛，这让他确信自己濒临死亡。

sentences.en: Now, it may be hypochondria.
sentences.zh: 现在，这可能是疑病症。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a massive hypochondria.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是一种严重的疑病症。

sentences.en: But he genuinely seems to have thought he was close to death.
sentences.zh: 但他似乎真的认为自己濒临死亡。

sentences.en: And I think he's exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我认为他精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: He's ill.
sentences.zh: 他病了。

sentences.en: People say he suggests he might have a hernia.
sentences.zh: 人们说他暗示自己可能患有疝气。

sentences.en: He might have gout.
sentences.zh: 他可能患有痛风。

sentences.en: I mean, I think he is genuinely ill.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为他确实病了。

sentences.en: And thrown into the mix is the fact that Keith has not congratulated him on his victory in capturing Le Genereau.
sentences.zh: 而且雪上加霜的是，基思并没有因为他俘获“热内罗号”的胜利而祝贺他。

sentences.en: And more than that, he has given it as a prize to his own lieutenants so that they will claim the prize money.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他还把这艘船作为奖品给了他自己的中尉，这样他们就能获得奖金。

sentences.en: And you can see why this would generate bad blood between the two men.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出为什么这会在两人之间产生积怨。

sentences.en: I mean, I think these are complicated waters, shall we say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这水很深，我们可以这么说。

sentences.en: And the upshot is, Keith and Nelson, you know, Keith has arrived, what, at the beginning of
sentences.zh: 结果就是，基思和纳尔逊，你知道，基思到达了，是在

sentences.en: They don't get on at all well.
sentences.zh: 他们相处得一点也不好。

sentences.en: There's constant arguments.
sentences.zh: 经常发生争吵。

sentences.en: Nelson, a lot of officers say Nelson's dallying with Lady Hamilton, doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊，很多军官说纳尔逊与汉密尔顿夫人调情，不在乎。

sentences.en: Other people say, no, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 其他人说，不，那没关系。

sentences.en: He's great.
sentences.zh: 他很棒。

sentences.en: It's all going well.
sentences.zh: 一切都很顺利。

sentences.en: But Nelson, by about the middle of the year, is constantly saying, I've had enough.
sentences.zh: 但纳尔逊到了年中左右，一直在说，我受够了。

sentences.en: I want to go home.
sentences.zh: 我想回家。

sentences.en: Please let me go home.
sentences.zh: 请让我回家。

sentences.en: And eventually, Keith says, yeah, fine.
sentences.zh: 最终，基思说，好吧，行。

sentences.en: You know, I'm sick of you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我厌倦你了。

sentences.en: Good riddance to you.
sentences.zh: 你走吧，不送。

sentences.en: And actually, even how the question of getting home, there's sort of an argument about that.
sentences.zh: 事实上，甚至关于回家的事，也有一种争论。

sentences.en: So Keith says to Nelson, I'll give you a frigate.
sentences.zh: 所以基思对纳尔逊说，我会给你一艘护卫舰。

sentences.en: You can go home in a frigate.
sentences.zh: 你可以坐护卫舰回家。

sentences.en: Now, Nelson says, oh, what a frigate.
sentences.zh: 现在，纳尔逊说，哦，什么护卫舰。

sentences.en: You know, I is a great star.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是一位伟大的明星。

sentences.en: The Hamiltons, these tremendous people, should be going home in splendor.
sentences.zh: 汉密尔顿夫妇，这些了不起的人，应该风光地回家。

sentences.en: And actually, as it turns out, Emma doesn't want to go by sea at all, does she?
sentences.zh: 事实上，结果证明，艾玛根本不想走海路，不是吗？

sentences.en: Partly because she knows that Maria Carolina, her great friend, is planning a trip to Vienna, great Habsburg capital.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是她知道她最好的朋友玛丽亚·卡罗琳娜正计划去维也纳，那个伟大的哈布斯堡王朝首都。

sentences.en: And she would really like to go on land with Maria Carolina.
sentences.zh: 她真的很想和玛丽亚·卡罗琳娜一起走陆路。

sentences.en: Now, as we will discover, Emma is also pregnant.
sentences.zh: 现在，正如我们将发现的那样，艾玛也怀孕了。

sentences.en: So that is another issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这是另一个问题。

sentences.en: Anyway, Nelson says, fine, you know, we'll go over land.
sentences.zh: 总之，纳尔逊说，好吧，你知道，我们走陆路。

sentences.en: We'll go via Austria.
sentences.zh: 我们经由奥地利。

sentences.en: We'll go via Germany and then, you know, cross the North Sea to England.
sentences.zh: 我们经由德国，然后，你知道，穿过北海去英国。

sentences.en: And I think there's a, do you not agree that this is seen as generally undignified?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有一个，你不觉得这通常被视为不得体吗？

sentences.en: Undignified.
sentences.zh: 不得体。

sentences.en: Yes, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意。

sentences.en: It's not fitting for the naval.
sentences.zh: 这不符合海军的身份。

sentences.en: Well, the guy who won the Battle of the Nile should come home, you know, land at Portsmouth, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 好吧，赢得尼罗河海战的人应该回家，你知道，在朴茨茅斯登陆，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: But actually, you know, there is a sense, I think, what Emma and Maria Carolina want,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你知道，我认为有一种感觉，艾玛和玛丽亚·卡罗琳娜想要什么，

sentences.en: Emma and Maria Carolina get with this.
sentences.zh: 艾玛和玛丽亚·卡罗琳娜就得到了什么。

sentences.en: And I think also there's a sense that he's been led into bad habits by foreigners bedecking him with baubles and comical medals and things.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为还有一种感觉，他被外国人带坏了，他们用小饰品、滑稽的奖章之类的东西装饰他。

sentences.en: He looks like a character from Gilbert and Sullivan, I think, at this point.
sentences.zh: 我认为他此时看起来就像吉尔伯特和沙利文歌剧里的角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, and this is felt to be kind of undignified.
sentences.zh: 是的，这被认为是一种不得体。

sentences.en: And I think this undoubtedly poisons the otherwise kind of complete mood of approbation that would be greeting him.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这无疑毒害了本应迎接他的那种完全赞许的氛围。

sentences.en: I think there is a kind of undertow of anxiety that he is making himself look ridiculous that he's letting himself down.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一种焦虑的暗流，觉得他让自己看起来很可笑，他在自毁形象。

sentences.en: And it obscures the fact that actually his term as commander in chief has not remotely been a disaster.
sentences.zh: 这掩盖了一个事实，即他担任总司令的任期绝非灾难。

sentences.en: So he's actually he has kept Sicily and in the fight, he's got Naples back and he's prosecuted
sentences.zh: 所以他实际上保持了西西里岛的战斗力，他夺回了那不勒斯，他以极高的效率执行了

sentences.en: the blockade of Malta with extreme efficiency and with such effectiveness that actually shortly after he's departed.
sentences.zh: 马耳他的封锁，效果如此显著，以至于在他离开后不久。

sentences.en: So on the 5th of September, 1800, Malta will surrender.
sentences.zh: 所以1800年9月5日，马耳他投降了。

sentences.en: And rather than hand it over to King Ferdinand, the British keep it, much to everyone's surprise.
sentences.zh: 英国人没有把它交给斐迪南国王，而是自己留下了，这让所有人都感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And basically they will keep it for, you know, for a century and more.
sentences.zh: 基本上他们会保留它一个世纪甚至更久。

sentences.en: It will play its part in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 它将在第二次世界大战中发挥作用。

sentences.en: But actually, the even bigger thing, surely, is that Nelson is returning to England as the victor of the Nile.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，更重要的事情当然是纳尔逊作为尼罗河海战的胜利者回到英国。

sentences.en: The winner of the greatest naval victory in Britain's history.
sentences.zh: 英国历史上最伟大的海军胜利的获胜者。

sentences.en: The victory that effectively punctured Napoleon's dreams of empire in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 这场胜利有效地粉碎了拿破仑在埃及的帝国梦想。

sentences.en: And the tragedy, I think, and this is even for his critics within the Navy, for Lord Keith
sentences.zh: 而悲剧在于，我认为，即使对于他在海军内部的批评者，对于基思勋爵

sentences.en: and all these other people, that as they see it, the tragedy is that the victor of the Nile has tarnished his own record and is going back.
sentences.zh: 和所有其他人来说，正如他们所见，悲剧在于尼罗河海战的胜利者玷污了自己的记录，并且正在回去。

sentences.en: You know, whether he's tarnished it, whether he really has tarnished it, I'm sure we can debate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他是否玷污了它，他是否真的玷污了它，我相信我们可以争论。

sentences.en: But the sadness is that he's not going back as the victor of the Nile.
sentences.zh: 但可悲的是，他不是作为尼罗河海战的胜利者回去的。

sentences.en: He's going back as a scandal-plagued, you know, controversy-haunted figure.
sentences.zh: 他是作为一个丑闻缠身、争议不断的形象回去的。

sentences.en: From Nelson's point of view, there is a positive to travelling over land, which is that obviously
sentences.zh: 从纳尔逊的角度来看，走陆路有一个积极的一面，那就是显然

sentences.en: he will have to go via Austria and other parts of Germany that are allied to Britain, all
sentences.zh: 他将不得不经由奥地利和德国其他与英国结盟的地区，

sentences.en: of whom are very excited by his achievement in defeating the French at the Battle of the Nile.
sentences.zh: 所有这些地区的人都对他击败法国人的尼罗河海战成就感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And so yet again, it promises opportunities for being praised by foreigners, which I think by this point, Nelson's very keen on.
sentences.zh: 所以再一次，这承诺了被外国人称赞的机会，我认为在这一点上，纳尔逊非常渴望。

sentences.en: By the time they get to, well, you know, we don't need to go through every single place they stopped at, but they go through Italy, Tuscany.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达时，好吧，你知道，我们不需要逐一列举他们停留的每一个地方，但他们穿过了意大利、托斯卡纳。

sentences.en: They end up in Austria and Vienna.
sentences.zh: 他们最终到达了奥地利和维也纳。

sentences.en: He goes to the theatre, he has his portrait painted.
sentences.zh: 他去剧院，他让人画了他的肖像。

sentences.en: He meets Joseph Haydn, who names a mass after him.
sentences.zh: 他见到了约瑟夫·海顿，海顿以他的名字命名了一部弥撒曲。

sentences.en: He's a big celebrity and everyone's very excited and they're wearing kind of Nelson fashions and stuff like that, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他是一位大名人，每个人都非常兴奋，他们穿着纳尔逊式的时装之类的东西，不是吗？

sentences.en: And Emma Hamilton fashions as well.
sentences.zh: 还有艾玛·汉密尔顿式的时装。

sentences.en: So she too is a big star.
sentences.zh: 所以她也是一位大明星。

sentences.en: You know, women in Vienna are copying her look as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，维也纳的女性也在模仿她的装扮。

sentences.en: They are being treated as stars and I think both of them absolutely adore it.
sentences.zh: 他们被当作明星对待，我认为他们俩都非常喜欢这种感觉。

sentences.en: I mean, I worked out how much this trip cost them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我算了一下这次旅行花了他们多少钱。

sentences.en: This trip cost them £3,000.
sentences.zh: 这次旅行花了他们3000英镑。

sentences.en: And if you compare that in income terms, that's about £5 million today.
sentences.zh: 如果你按收入水平来比较，那相当于今天的500万英镑左右。

sentences.en: That's a very expensive trip and that's money that they don't really have.
sentences.zh: 那是一次非常昂贵的旅行，而且那是他们并没有真正拥有的钱。

sentences.en: So there's that issue.
sentences.zh: 所以问题就在这儿。

sentences.en: The second issue, Emma heavily pregnant, as you mentioned, and people are already gossiping that Nelson may be the father.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是，正如你提到的，艾玛已经身怀六甲，人们已经在私下议论纳尔逊可能是孩子的父亲了。

sentences.en: He is the father.
sentences.zh: 他确实是父亲。

sentences.en: Their child was conceived while they were cruising, I think, off Malta in the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 我想，他们的孩子是在地中海马耳他附近航行时怀上的。

sentences.en: And I think it's in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得是在维也纳。

sentences.en: You get the sense it's in Vienna that he first notices Nelson is not a man who enjoys being laughed at.
sentences.zh: 你会感觉到，正是在维也纳，他第一次注意到纳尔逊不是一个喜欢被人嘲笑的人。

sentences.en: And it's clear that it's about now that people do start to laugh at him.
sentences.zh: 很明显，也就是从这时候起，人们开始嘲笑他了。

sentences.en: There are reports of him at balls, at banquets and things.
sentences.zh: 有报道说他在舞会、宴会等场合出现。

sentences.en: Emma's chattering away, as she always does.
sentences.zh: 艾玛像往常一样喋喋不休。

sentences.en: And he's standing there sort of silent.
sentences.zh: 而他站在那里，显得有些沉默。

sentences.en: And I think I have a sort of sense of him, you know, glancing over his shoulder and noticing people laughing behind their hands.
sentences.zh: 我似乎能感觉到他，你知道，他会回头看，注意到人们在掩嘴偷笑。

sentences.en: And he doesn't like it.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Well, I think also, particularly in Vienna, he's meeting with very high-born British aristocrats who, of course, are contemptuous of Emma, basically, for being a barmaid.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我也认为，特别是在维也纳，他接触的都是出身高贵的英国贵族，他们当然打心底里瞧不起艾玛，因为她毕竟是个酒吧女招待。

sentences.en: Nelson has his friend, Lord Minto, who's there, who says, you know, unbelievably coarse, appalling, vulgar woman.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊的朋友明托勋爵也在场，他说，你知道，这女人粗俗不堪、令人震惊、毫无教养。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And while Emma was in Italy, you know, her Lancastrian accent had no cut through with the Italians.
sentences.zh: 当艾玛在意大利时，你知道，她那兰开夏郡的口音在意大利人面前根本行不通。

sentences.en: I mean, it meant nothing to them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对他们来说那毫无意义。

sentences.en: But now he's being reintegrated into high society, English high society.
sentences.zh: 但现在他正重新融入上流社会，英国的上流社会。

sentences.en: All those reserves of snobbery are kind of waiting to come out again.
sentences.zh: 那些势利眼的积怨似乎又要爆发了。

sentences.en: Well, the issue of manners and showiness starts to become a real issue the further north they go.
sentences.zh: 嗯，随着他们越往北走，礼仪和炫耀的问题就开始变得真正棘手起来。

sentences.en: So, for example, when they get to Prague or to Dresden, there are British visitors, British
sentences.zh: 例如，当他们到达布拉格或德累斯顿时，那些英国游客、英国

sentences.en: aristocrats or diplomats, who then start writing back to London saying, God, they're absolutely ghastly.
sentences.zh: 贵族或外交官，就开始写信回伦敦说，天哪，他们简直太糟糕了。

sentences.en: So, here's an example.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有个例子。

sentences.en: Lady Hamilton declared she was passionately fond of champagne, took such a portion of it as astonished me.
sentences.zh: 汉密尔顿夫人宣称她酷爱香槟，喝下的分量让我大吃一惊。

sentences.en: Lord Nelson was not behindhand, calling more vociferously than usual for songs in his own praise.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊勋爵也不甘示弱，比平时更大声地要求人们唱赞美他的歌。

sentences.en: Now, that, to me, does actually ring true, because Nelson does like a lot of praise.
sentences.zh: 现在，这对我来说确实听起来很真实，因为纳尔逊确实喜欢被人吹捧。

sentences.en: And Lady Hamilton, you feel, is not a woman who's going to stop drinking champagne just because she's pregnant, or so.
sentences.zh: 而你会觉得，汉密尔顿夫人绝不是那种会因为怀孕就停止喝香槟的女人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And I think, I mean, even now in England, there is a sense that you shouldn't be the first to call for a song in your own praise.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，即使在今天的英国，人们也觉得你不应该第一个要求别人唱赞美自己的歌。

sentences.en: So, if you did that at a Rest is History dinner, I would be...
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在《历史的余味》晚餐会上这么做，我会……

sentences.en: Dominic, I would never do that.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我绝不会那样做。

sentences.en: I mean, the one thing actually this podcast is not known for is self-congratulation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个播客最不以自我吹嘘而闻名。

sentences.en: People often criticise us for too much humility.
sentences.zh: 人们经常批评我们过于谦虚。

sentences.en: I think on this one level, we have behaved better than Nelson.
sentences.zh: 我想在这一点上，我们表现得比纳尔逊好。

sentences.en: However, we must always bear in mind that he did defeat the French at the Battle of the
sentences.zh: 然而，我们必须时刻记住，他确实在尼罗河海战中击败了法国人，

sentences.en: Nile, and he did secure Malta for the Royal Navy, so...
sentences.zh: 他也确实为皇家海军保住了马耳他，所以……

sentences.en: You're desperate to hammer home this Malta point on you, I can tell.
sentences.zh: 我看得出来，你非常想强调马耳他这一点。

sentences.en: Well, it's so important, and it's overlooked.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这太重要了，而且一直被忽视。

sentences.en: Anyway, they travel through Europe, they get to Germany, and they catch a boat back to Yarmouth.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们穿过欧洲，到达德国，然后乘船回到雅茅斯。

sentences.en: It's a packet boat.
sentences.zh: 那是一艘邮船。

sentences.en: It's not, you know, a great ship of the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那可不是皇家海军的巨舰。

sentences.en: However, when Nelson lands, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 然而，当纳尔逊登陆时，这并不重要。

sentences.en: He's greeted, you know, the returning hero, right?
sentences.zh: 他受到了欢迎，你知道，是凯旋的英雄，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, there are huge crowds.
sentences.zh: 是的，有大批人群。

sentences.en: It's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But, at the back of his mind, surely, he's got his heavily pregnant mistress and her elderly husband, and that's a slightly odd menage with which to return to...
sentences.zh: 但是，在他内心深处，肯定在想，他带着身怀六甲的情妇和她年迈的丈夫，这是一种有点奇怪的组合，带着他们回到……

sentences.en: Just to explain for people who aren't familiar with the geography of East Anglia, Yarmouth
sentences.zh: 给那些不熟悉东安格利亚地理的人解释一下，雅茅斯

sentences.en: is the nearest port to the vicarage where both Fanny and Nelson's father are waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 是离牧师住宅最近的港口，范妮和纳尔逊的父亲都在那里等着他。

sentences.en: Or are they, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 真的是这样吗，多米尼克？

sentences.en: Because there's kind of a mix-up, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 因为中间出了点乱子，不是吗？

sentences.en: There's a massive mix-up, because actually Fanny has also got him a country house called
sentences.zh: 确实出了大乱子，因为实际上范妮也为他准备了一处叫

sentences.en: Roundwood, which is in Suffolk, which she's been preparing.
sentences.zh: 圆木的乡间别墅，在萨福克郡，她一直在筹备。

sentences.en: They never live at it, as it turns out.
sentences.zh: 结果他们从来没住过那里。

sentences.en: And there's a great confusion.
sentences.zh: 而且造成了很大的混乱。

sentences.en: Are they going to meet there?
sentences.zh: 他们是要在那里见面吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to meet in London?
sentences.zh: 他们是要在伦敦见面吗？

sentences.en: Fanny's down in London.
sentences.zh: 范妮在伦敦。

sentences.en: Nelson goes to the house.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊去了那栋房子。

sentences.en: There's nobody there.
sentences.zh: 那里一个人也没有。

sentences.en: He's very offended.
sentences.zh: 他感到非常受冒犯。

sentences.en: You can imagine Nelson.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象纳尔逊的样子。

sentences.en: He's used to flattery.
sentences.zh: 他习惯了阿谀奉承。

sentences.en: He's used to being the centre of attention.
sentences.zh: 他习惯了成为关注的焦点。

sentences.en: He arrives at the house, and there's no one there to greet him.
sentences.zh: 他到达房子时，却没有人迎接他。

sentences.en: Anyway, Fanny has been waiting all this time.
sentences.zh: 总之，范妮一直在等。

sentences.en: And to remind people about Fanny, Fanny is very shy, kind of quiet.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下大家，范妮非常害羞，性格安静。

sentences.en: If you had to criticise Fanny, which I hate to do, but I will force myself.
sentences.zh: 如果你非要批评范妮，虽然我不愿意，但我会强迫自己。

sentences.en: For the good of the podcast, she's perhaps a little bit boring.
sentences.zh: 为了播客的效果，她可能有点无聊。

sentences.en: He married her in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 他在加勒比海娶了她。

sentences.en: They came home to England.
sentences.zh: 他们回到了英国。

sentences.en: He nursed her when he was injured.
sentences.zh: 他受伤时是她照顾的。

sentences.en: She's become a second daughter to his father.
sentences.zh: 她成了他父亲的第二个女儿。

sentences.en: And Fanny has become increasingly anxious in recent months.
sentences.zh: 近几个月来，范妮变得越来越焦虑。

sentences.en: Nelson's letters have, A, started to dry up.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊的信，首先，开始变少了。

sentences.en: But B, when they do come, they are very short and they are very cold.
sentences.zh: 其次，即使有信寄来，也写得很短，而且非常冷淡。

sentences.en: And she says to her friends, I'm actually quite worried about these Hamiltons.
sentences.zh: 她对朋友们说，我其实很担心这些汉密尔顿一家。

sentences.en: There's a clear sense of kind of growing dread in Fanny's mind about the influence of the
sentences.zh: 范妮心中有一种明显的恐惧感，担心汉密尔顿一家的

sentences.en: Hamiltons.
sentences.zh: 影响。

sentences.en: Now, we're not going to degenerate into Team Emma and Team Fanny, are we, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们不会沦落到分成“艾玛队”和“范妮队”吧？

sentences.en: I hope.
sentences.zh: 我希望不会。

sentences.en: I've always mentioned Mansfield Park at the start of this episode, Jane Austen's novel.
sentences.zh: 我在本集开头提到了简·奥斯汀的小说《曼斯菲尔德庄园》。

sentences.en: Jane Austen, of course, had a brother who served in the Royal Navy, kept very abreast of Nelsoniana.
sentences.zh: 简·奥斯汀当然有个在皇家海军服役的哥哥，对纳尔逊的事迹非常了解。

sentences.en: And I've always wondered whether Fanny Price in Mansfield Park, who is the, you know, the slightly mousy, slightly, you know, the poor relation, not showy at all.
sentences.zh: 我一直想知道《曼斯菲尔德庄园》里的范妮·普莱斯，那个你知道的，有点胆小、有点贫穷的亲戚，一点也不张扬的人，是否就是原型。

sentences.en: And she's counterpointed to a much more glamorous woman in the form of Mary Crawford.
sentences.zh: 她与玛丽·克劳福德那种更迷人的女性形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: And I've always wondered if there's a little hint there, perhaps, of the dynamic between
sentences.zh: 我一直怀疑这里面是否有一点暗示，关于

sentences.en: Fanny, Nelson's wife, and Emma, Nelson's mistress.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊的妻子范妮和纳尔逊的情妇艾玛之间的动态。

sentences.en: Well, it feels like a very Jane Austen dynamic, generally, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这感觉非常像简·奥斯汀式的动态，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 皇家海军一直在封锁法国海岸，试图切断法国的贸易和补给。

sentences.en: And in the long run, in the very, very long run, that's how we win the war.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，非常非常长远来看，这就是我们赢得战争的方式。

sentences.en: Because we control the seas, we suffocate Napoleon, suffocate his economy, and we force him into mad gambles like invading Russia.
sentences.zh: 因为我们控制了海洋，我们窒息了拿破仑，窒息了他的经济，并迫使他进行像入侵俄罗斯那样的疯狂赌博。

sentences.en: Sad to say, not all of our European friends have respected this blockade.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，并非我们所有的欧洲朋友都尊重这种封锁。

sentences.en: And a very good example is Denmark.
sentences.zh: 丹麦就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Denmark has been flirting with a policy of armed neutrality, meaning they send warships to help their merchant ships break the blockade.
sentences.zh: 丹麦一直在尝试武装中立政策，这意味着他们派遣军舰帮助他们的商船突破封锁。

sentences.en: And then in late 1800, while Nelson is in the middle of the sort of Fannie-Emma imbroglio, there is a shocking new development.
sentences.zh: 然后在1800年底，当纳尔逊正处于范妮和艾玛的纠葛之中时，出现了一个令人震惊的新进展。

sentences.en: So one of our key, Britain's key second coalition allies, was Tsar Paul I of Russia.
sentences.zh: 英国第二次反法同盟的关键盟友之一是俄罗斯沙皇保罗一世。

sentences.en: He is a very strange and disagreeable man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常古怪且令人不快的人。

sentences.en: We like a strange and disagreeable Tsar, don't we?
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢古怪且令人不快的沙皇，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, we specialize in them, as does Russia.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们很擅长对付他们，俄罗斯也是。

sentences.en: And he has, I think, he's sort of got all the worst aspects of Peter the Great and none of the good ones.
sentences.zh: 我想他身上有彼得大帝所有最糟糕的方面，却没有一个好的方面。

sentences.en: So he loves massive military parades.
sentences.zh: 他热爱大规模的军事阅兵。

sentences.en: He loves flogging people.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢鞭打人。

sentences.en: He's obsessed with, so Peter the Great, people may remember, was obsessed with beards and cutting people's, you know, stopping them wearing caftans and they had to wear trousers.
sentences.zh: 他很痴迷，大家可能还记得，彼得大帝痴迷于胡须，剪掉人们的胡子，你知道，阻止他们穿长袍，他们必须穿裤子。

sentences.en: This guy, he doesn't approve of modern liberal clothing.
sentences.zh: 这家伙，他不赞成现代自由主义的服装。

sentences.en: He, in fact, bans round hats, trousers and lace-up shoes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他禁止圆顶礼帽、裤子和系带鞋。

sentences.en: And he also believes that waistcoats contributed to the outbreak of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 他还认为背心导致了法国大革命的爆发。

sentences.en: Because he thinks all of these things are kind of liberal, it's liberal coded dress.
sentences.zh: 因为他认为所有这些东西都是某种自由主义的，是带有自由主义色彩的服装。

sentences.en: And it speaks of Republican sympathies.
sentences.zh: 这代表了共和主义的倾向。

sentences.en: And he just doesn't like Republicanism.
sentences.zh: 他就是不喜欢共和主义。

sentences.en: He doesn't like new ideas.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢新思想。

sentences.en: There's all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 就是这些乱七八糟的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, which is why, obviously, why he would be fighting against France.
sentences.zh: 所以，很明显，这就是他为什么会与法国作战的原因。

sentences.en: Because France is a hotbed of waistcoats and ludicrous hats.
sentences.zh: 因为法国是背心和荒谬帽子的温床。

sentences.en: But there's another side to him.
sentences.zh: 但他还有另一面。

sentences.en: He's obsessed with becoming, I mean, this is your Malta thing again, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他痴迷于成为，我是说，这又是你的马耳他问题了，汤姆。

sentences.en: He's like you.
sentences.zh: 他就像你一样。

sentences.en: He's obsessed with becoming the Grand Master of the Knights of St. John.
sentences.zh: 他痴迷于成为圣约翰骑士团的大团长。

sentences.en: So, when Britain did capture Malta in September 1800 and kept Malta for themselves, Tsar Paul I said, what?
sentences.zh: 所以，当英国在1800年9月占领马耳他并将其据为己有时，沙皇保罗一世说，什么？

sentences.en: You know, what's this?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: You can't have Malta.
sentences.zh: 你不能占有马耳他。

sentences.en: And switches sides.
sentences.zh: 于是他倒戈了。

sentences.en: So, you see, I'm right.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，我是对的。

sentences.en: Malta is key.
sentences.zh: 马耳他是关键。

sentences.en: You see, I think it's sad that we had to fight the Danes.
sentences.zh: 你看，我觉得我们不得不与丹麦人作战很可悲。

sentences.en: We had to crush, we had to teach the Danes a lesson.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不粉碎他们，我们不得不给丹麦人一个教训。

sentences.en: And this would not have happened if we hadn't taken Malta.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有占领马耳他，这一切就不会发生。

sentences.en: Anyway, basically, Paul switches sides.
sentences.zh: 总之，基本上，保罗倒戈了。

sentences.en: He opens talks with Bonaparte.
sentences.zh: 他与波拿巴开启了谈判。

sentences.en: And Bonaparte, by this point, is first consul, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而波拿巴此时已经是第一执政了，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, he's overthrown the Directory.
sentences.zh: 所以，他推翻了督政府。

sentences.en: He's clearly basically the dictator now.
sentences.zh: 他显然基本上已经是独裁者了。

sentences.en: So, in December 1800, Paul signed a deal with the other Baltic powers.
sentences.zh: 所以，在1800年12月，保罗与其他波罗的海国家签署了一项协议。

sentences.en: That's Denmark, Sweden, and Prussia.
sentences.zh: 那是丹麦、瑞典和普鲁士。

sentences.en: And they set up a League of Armed Neutrality.
sentences.zh: 他们建立了武装中立联盟。

sentences.en: They will break the blockade of the Royal Navy, and they will trade with the French.
sentences.zh: 他们将打破皇家海军的封锁，并与法国人进行贸易。

sentences.en: Now, clearly, this is a massive threat to Britain's war effort.
sentences.zh: 现在，很明显，这对英国的战争努力是一个巨大的威胁。

sentences.en: First of all, it would mean that Russia controls the Baltic.
sentences.zh: 首先，这意味着俄罗斯控制了波罗的海。

sentences.en: But also, it would give the French enough timber, enough hemp, enough iron to restock their navy, build loads of new ships, win back control of the seas, potentially.
sentences.zh: 但同时，这也将给法国人提供足够的木材、大麻、铁，让他们重新装备海军，建造大量新船，并有可能夺回海洋控制权。

sentences.en: Of course, if they did that, it's curtains for Britain and game over in the war.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果他们那样做了，英国就完了，战争也就结束了。

sentences.en: So, to quote Andrew Lambert, great historian, if Britain accepted, she would abandon her great power status and accept French hegemony over Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以，引用伟大的历史学家安德鲁·兰伯特的话，如果英国接受这一点，她将放弃她的大国地位，并接受法国在欧洲的霸权。

sentences.en: These issues were fundamental to Britain's very survival.
sentences.zh: 这些问题对英国的生存至关重要。

sentences.en: So, by December 1800, to the point at which Nelson is going off to William Beckford's slightly sordid party,
sentences.zh: 所以，到了1800年12月，也就是纳尔逊要去参加威廉·贝克福德那场稍微有些肮脏的派对时，

sentences.en: George III is telling the House of Commons, our honour and independence, our maritime interests, our security, all depend on not letting this happen.
sentences.zh: 乔治三世正在告诉下议院，我们的荣誉和独立、我们的海上利益、我们的安全，都取决于不能让这种情况发生。

sentences.en: And this is upsetting for him, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这让他很心烦，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's got kind of, you know, he's related to the Danish royal family.
sentences.zh: 因为他，你知道，他和丹麦王室有亲戚关系。

sentences.en: He loves the Danes.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢丹麦人。

sentences.en: So, Denmark, since 1784, has been run not by its king, because he's mad, but by his son, Crown Prince Frederick.
sentences.zh: 所以，自1784年以来，丹麦一直不是由国王统治的，因为他疯了，而是由他的儿子，王储弗雷德里克统治的。

sentences.en: And Crown Prince Frederick is George III's nephew.
sentences.zh: 而王储弗雷德里克是乔治三世的侄子。

sentences.en: And George likes him.
sentences.zh: 乔治喜欢他。

sentences.en: He likes the Danes.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢丹麦人。

sentences.en: Everybody likes the Danes.
sentences.zh: 每个人都喜欢丹麦人。

sentences.en: So, Nelson, he sees them as basically the best thing any foreigner can be, the brothers of Englishmen.
sentences.zh: 所以，纳尔逊，他认为他们基本上是外国人所能成为的最好的存在，是英国人的兄弟。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: High praise.
sentences.zh: 高度赞扬。

sentences.en: It was the highest praise.
sentences.zh: 这是最高的赞扬。

sentences.en: So, they tried to negotiate, but while that's happening, the Emirati says, look, we're going to have to send a fleet into the Baltic to show that we mean business.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们试图进行谈判，但在谈判进行的同时，海军部说，看，我们必须派遣一支舰队进入波罗的海，以表明我们是认真的。

sentences.en: And your orders are, capture or destroy the Danish fleet firSt.
sentences.zh: 你的命令是，首先俘获或摧毁丹麦舰队。

sentences.en: Because obviously, if we're sailing up the Baltic, Denmark comes first, then you go past Sweden, and then finally you get to Russia.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，如果我们航行进入波罗的海，首先是丹麦，然后经过瑞典，最后才能到达俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And, you know, the orders are very clear.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，命令非常明确。

sentences.en: The Secretary of War, Henry Dundas, writes, we must show the Royal Navy is, and I quote, a match for the whole naval force of the world combined.
sentences.zh: 战争大臣亨利·邓达斯写道，我们必须展示皇家海军，引用他的原话，是“世界上所有海军力量的总和的对手”。

sentences.en: We have to rule the waves because we're so inconsequential on land that, you know, that's the only way we'll stay in this war.
sentences.zh: 我们必须统治海洋，因为我们在陆地上实在无足轻重，你知道，这是我们能继续这场战争的唯一途径。

sentences.en: Now, this is made for Nelson, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这简直是为纳尔逊量身定做的，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, this has got his name all over it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这上面到处都是他的影子。

sentences.en: And he has been itching to get to sea.
sentences.zh: 而且他一直渴望出海。

sentences.en: The weird thing is, he begged to be sent back to England, begged and begged and made a nuisance of himself to Admiral Lord Keith.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，他曾恳求被送回英国，苦苦哀求，甚至让基思海军上将感到厌烦。

sentences.en: Then he got back to England and said, I can't wait to get back to sea again.
sentences.zh: 然后他回到英国又说，我迫不及待想再次出海了。

sentences.en: Because, of course, he's adrift on land, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，他在陆地上就像漂泊无依，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's not at ease, and he's got this terrible love triangle.
sentences.zh: 他感到不安，而且还陷入了这段糟糕的三角恋。

sentences.en: Well, I think also going and having a crack at the Danes,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我也认为去教训一下丹麦人，

sentences.en: it's simpler than having to arse around with Malta and, you know,
sentences.zh: 比在马耳他那些破事上瞎折腾要简单，你知道，

sentences.en: Queens and all that.
sentences.zh: 还有女王什么的。

sentences.en: It's much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 那要复杂得多。

sentences.en: But I think the fact that Nelson is not appointed to the command, he's only given a role as deputy,
sentences.zh: 但我认为纳尔逊没有被任命为总指挥，只给了他一个副职，

sentences.en: does reflect the fact that back in London, his reputation has been tarnished.
sentences.zh: 确实反映了他在伦敦的名声已经受损的事实。

sentences.en: I think otherwise he would have been given command of it.
sentences.zh: 我想否则他本会被授予指挥权的。

sentences.en: I think it has.
sentences.zh: 我想确实如此。

sentences.en: Whether he would be capable of actually wielding sole command is an interesting question because he's, I mean, not for the first or the last time,
sentences.zh: 至于他是否有能力真正独当一面是一个有趣的问题，因为他，我的意思是，这也不是第一次也不是最后一次，

sentences.en: he's in a bit of a terrible state, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他现在的状态很糟糕，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's had an attack of malarial fever.
sentences.zh: 他患上了疟疾。

sentences.en: I always think with Nelson, so much of this physical stuff is psychosomatic to some degree.
sentences.zh: 我总觉得对于纳尔逊来说，很多身体上的问题在某种程度上是心因性的。

sentences.en: You know, he went to see his old patron, Sir John Jervis, who's now the Earl of St. Vincent.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他去见了老恩人约翰·杰维斯爵士，也就是现在的圣文森特伯爵。

sentences.en: And Jervis was really shocked by Nelson's appearance.
sentences.zh: 杰维斯对纳尔逊的样子感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: Poor man, he is devoured with vanity, weakness, and folly.
sentences.zh: 可怜的人，他被虚荣、软弱和愚蠢所吞噬。

sentences.en: Well, that's what you want from the patron and father figure that you most admire in the Navy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是你从海军中最敬仰的恩人和父亲形象那里得到的评价。

sentences.en: From there, Nelson travels down to the dockyard at Plymouth and there he has news at the end of January, beginning of February, that changes his life.
sentences.zh: 从那里，纳尔逊前往普利茅斯的船坞，在一月底或二月初，他得到了一个改变他一生的消息。

sentences.en: Because probably on the 29th of January, we can't be sure,
sentences.zh: 因为大概是在1月29日，我们无法确定，

sentences.en: Emma has finally given birth to a daughter.
sentences.zh: 艾玛终于生下了一个女儿。

sentences.en: Do they acknowledge it?
sentences.zh: 他们承认了吗？

sentences.en: They don't.
sentences.zh: 他们没有。

sentences.en: Well, they can't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们不能。

sentences.en: How can you?
sentences.zh: 怎么能呢？

sentences.en: Are they so subtle that they give no hint as to whose daughter it might have been?
sentences.zh: 他们是否隐晦到连暗示一下这可能是谁的女儿都不肯？

sentences.en: They call her Horatia.
sentences.zh: 他们给她取名叫霍拉蒂娅。

sentences.en: Horatia, yeah.
sentences.zh: 霍拉蒂娅，是的。

sentences.en: And he sends Emma all these coded letters.
sentences.zh: 他给艾玛发了所有这些加密信件。

sentences.en: They call themselves Mr. and Mrs. Thompson.
sentences.zh: 他们自称汤普森先生和夫人。

sentences.en: And, I mean, this is the best thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，这是最绝的。

sentences.en: Nelson wrote to her and he said, I think what would be really nice is if you, when you do the birth certificate, the name of the parents should be
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊写信给她说，我觉得如果当你填写出生证明时，父母的名字写成这样会很不错：

sentences.en: Johem and Maratha Etnorb.
sentences.zh: Johem 和 Maratha Etnorb。

sentences.en: Etnorb Bronte.
sentences.zh: Etnorb 就是 Bronte（勃朗特）。

sentences.en: This is a quote.
sentences.zh: 这是引用。

sentences.en: If you read the surname backwards and take the letters of the other names, it gives the names of Horatio and Emma Bronte.
sentences.zh: 如果你把姓氏倒过来读，再取其他名字的字母，就是霍拉蒂奥和艾玛·勃朗特的名字。

sentences.en: This is him showing off about his dukedom.
sentences.zh: 这是他在炫耀自己的公爵头衔。

sentences.en: And that's classic Nelson.
sentences.zh: 这很纳尔逊。

sentences.en: It's the sort of, he thinks he's being really subtle, but he obviously is just, it's laughable.
sentences.zh: 他以为自己表现得很含蓄，但显然这只是，太可笑了。

sentences.en: But he's also boasting.
sentences.zh: 但他也在吹嘘。

sentences.en: Yeah, he wants to draw attention to it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他想引起人们的注意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So for the time being, this little girl is given to a woman called Mrs. Gibson.
sentences.zh: 所以暂时，这个小女孩被交给了吉布森夫人照顾。

sentences.en: And Mrs. Gibson basically acts as her guardian, doesn't she?
sentences.zh: 吉布森夫人基本上充当了她的监护人，对吧？

sentences.en: And obviously this massively intensifies the bond between Nelson and Emma, because Fanny hadn't been able to give him a child.
sentences.zh: 显然这极大地加强了纳尔逊和艾玛之间的纽带，因为范妮没能为他生下孩子。

sentences.en: And Nelson loves children.
sentences.zh: 而纳尔逊很爱孩子。

sentences.en: So he'd be very besotted with Horatio.
sentences.zh: 所以他会对霍拉蒂娅非常痴迷。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: And actually, I think it's the fact that he's had the child and he can't see her contributes to his misery, because these are some of the lowest weeks of his life.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我认为正是因为他有了孩子却无法见到她，才加剧了他的痛苦，因为这是他一生中最灰暗的几周。

sentences.en: He's stuck in this new ship, the St. George in Torbay.
sentences.zh: 他被困在托贝的新船“圣乔治号”上。

sentences.en: The weather at the beginning of 1801 is absolutely terrible.
sentences.zh: 1801年初的天气简直糟糕透了。

sentences.en: It's kind of howling gales, driving rain, there's snowstorms and stuff.
sentences.zh: 狂风呼啸，大雨倾盆，还有暴风雪之类的。

sentences.en: He's in this cabin on his own.
sentences.zh: 他独自待在这个船舱里。

sentences.en: He's really low.
sentences.zh: 他情绪非常低落。

sentences.en: The newspapers are full of kind of gossip about him.
sentences.zh: 报纸上到处都是关于他的流言蜚语。

sentences.en: There are cartoons that basically show Emma drinking gin, massively pregnant.
sentences.zh: 有些漫画基本上画的是艾玛挺着大肚子在喝杜松子酒。

sentences.en: So there's a famous one of Emma as Dido, the Queen of Carthage, who gets abandoned by Aeneas, who sails off.
sentences.zh: 有一幅很有名的画，画的是艾玛扮演迦太基女王狄多，被扬帆远去的埃涅阿斯抛弃。

sentences.en: And it's grotesquely unfair.
sentences.zh: 这非常不公平。

sentences.en: And of course, is very much drawing attention to the fact that she's pregnant.
sentences.zh: 当然，这很大程度上是在强调她怀孕的事实。

sentences.en: And so everybody knows what's going on.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: She's very large in these cartoons.
sentences.zh: 在这些漫画里她显得非常臃肿。

sentences.en: And Sir William Hamilton often pops up in them, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 威廉·汉密尔顿爵士也经常出现在画里，不是吗？

sentences.en: Looking very beaky and weedy in the background.
sentences.zh: 在背景里看起来尖嘴猴腮、萎靡不振。

sentences.en: Wizen.
sentences.zh: 枯槁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so very pervy.
sentences.zh: 而且非常猥琐。

sentences.zh: 关于纳尔逊的另一件事，我发现既可悲又可笑，那就是他被嫉妒折磨得死去活来。

sentences.zh: 在霍拉蒂娅出生几天后，

sentences.zh: 艾玛写信告诉他：

sentences.en: I'm going to have dinner with the Prince of Wales, the future George IV.
sentences.zh: 我要和威尔士亲王，也就是未来的乔治四世共进晚餐。

sentences.en: And Nelson, this is the worst news he's ever heard.
sentences.zh: 对纳尔逊来说，这是他听过的最糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: Because the Prince Regent's a massive lech, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为摄政王是个大色狼，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 摄政王确实是个糟糕透顶的人。

sentences.en: And Nelson writes back, he says, I know his aim is to have you for a mistress.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊回信说，我知道他的目的是想让你做他的情妇。

sentences.en: The thought so agitates me that I cannot write.
sentences.zh: 这个念头让我心烦意乱，以至于无法写信。

sentences.en: I'm in tears.
sentences.zh: 我泪流满面。

sentences.en: I cannot bear it.
sentences.zh: 我无法忍受。

sentences.zh: 像这样的内容还有很多，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 他就是没完没了地写这些。

sentences.zh: 这个播客可以讲上几个小时。

sentences.en: They're comical, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实挺滑稽的。

sentences.en: Do not let him touch you, nor sit next to you.
sentences.zh: 不要让他碰你，也不要坐在他旁边。

sentences.en: If he comes, get up.
sentences.zh: 如果他来了，就站起来。

sentences.en: And I was dead.
sentences.zh: 我当时心如死灰。

sentences.en: Oh God, why do I live?
sentences.zh: 哦上帝，我为什么还要活着？

sentences.en: But the brilliant thing is, is that he's having to do the same with Emma, because Emma's massively jealous of him.
sentences.zh: 但绝妙的是，他不得不对艾玛也这样做，因为艾玛对他也非常嫉妒。

sentences.en: So I think he goes to Portsmouth, and he's had to swear to Emma that he will spend no time with other women.
sentences.zh: 我想他去了朴茨茅斯，不得不向艾玛发誓他不会和其他女人在一起。

sentences.en: And of course he finds that he does.
sentences.zh: 当然他发现自己还是会遇到。

sentences.en: And so he writes back and confesses.
sentences.zh: 于是他回信坦白。

sentences.en: So he describes one woman as dressed old ewe lamb fashion.
sentences.zh: 他形容其中一个女人穿着“老母羊装嫩”。

sentences.en: So mutton dressed as lamb.
sentences.zh: 也就是老气横秋却装扮年轻。

sentences.en: Another looks like a cook maid.
sentences.zh: 另一个看起来像个厨娘。

sentences.en: Another likes a drop.
sentences.zh: 另一个喜欢喝两杯。

sentences.zh: 还有一个55岁，又聋又满脸天花疤。

sentences.en: Oh, such gallantry.
sentences.zh: 哦，真是风度翩翩。

sentences.en: And, and kind of mutual jealousy, again, is seems to be kind of part of the rocket fuel of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 这种相互的嫉妒，似乎又是他们关系中的助燃剂。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.zh: 我想是这样。

sentences.en: This is sort of a possessiveness and a paranoia combined.
sentences.zh: 这是一种占有欲和偏执的结合。

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, what's happened to Fanny?
sentences.zh: 那么，与此同时，范妮怎么样了？

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: Fanny has not given up hope entirely.
sentences.zh: 范妮并没有完全放弃希望。

sentences.en: That's the sad thing.
sentences.zh: 这才是最可悲的。

sentences.en: So she's heard from her son,
sentences.zh: 她从她儿子那里听说了，

sentences.en: Josiah.
sentences.zh: 约西亚。

sentences.en: Listeners may remember,
sentences.zh: 听众可能还记得，

sentences.en: saving Nelson's life and the attack on Tenerife when he lost his arm.
sentences.zh: 在特内里费岛的袭击中，他救了纳尔逊的命，当时纳尔逊失去了手臂。

sentences.en: Anyway, she's heard from Josiah that Nelson's eye infection has come back.
sentences.zh: 总之，她从约西亚那里听说纳尔逊的眼疾复发了。

sentences.en: And Fanny writes and she says,
sentences.zh: 范妮写信说：

sentences.en: I'd like to come and I'll be your affectionate nurse and look after you.
sentences.zh: 我想过去，我会做你深情的护士，照顾你。

sentences.en: And Nelson replies.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊回信了。

sentences.en: You said Nelson behaves quite cruelly.
sentences.zh: 你说纳尔逊表现得相当残忍。

sentences.en: I think this is very cruel actually from Nelson.
sentences.zh: 我觉得纳尔逊这封信确实非常残忍。

sentences.en: He replies to her with an extraordinarily savage letter at the end of February.
sentences.zh: 他在二月底回了一封极其冷酷的信。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说：

sentences.en: I'm going to pay you an allowance of 400 pounds a quarter.
sentences.zh: 我每季度会给你400英镑的津贴。

sentences.en: And that is it.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: And I'm going to cut you off from this point onwards.
sentences.zh: 从现在起，我要和你断绝关系。

sentences.en: I only wish people would never mention my name to you.
sentences.zh: 我只希望人们永远不要在你面前提起我的名字。

sentences.en: I want neither nursing nor attention.
sentences.zh: 我既不需要护理，也不需要关心。

sentences.en: Had you come here, I should not have gone on shore, nor would you have come afloat.
sentences.zh: 如果你来了，我也不会上岸，你也不会上船。

sentences.en: You know, even if you'd come, I wouldn't even see you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即使你来了，我也根本不会见你。

sentences.en: I don't, I don't want to think about you anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不想，我不想再想到你了。

sentences.en: I just want you out of my life.
sentences.zh: 我只想让你从我的生活中消失。

sentences.en: So you talked about Nelson being cruel.
sentences.zh: 所以你谈到了纳尔逊的残忍。

sentences.en: Emma also by this point is behaving abominably to Fanny, kind of turning Nelson's family against her, calling her names, kind of gossiping about her behind her back.
sentences.zh: 艾玛此时对范妮的行为也极其恶劣，挑拨纳尔逊的家人反对她，辱骂她，在背后说她的坏话。

sentences.en: And I think both of them have kind of been driven mad by their mutual passion, but also by the social pressure that it has put both of them under.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们俩都被彼此的激情冲昏了头脑，同时也受到了社会压力的影响。

sentences.en: And I think this is the kind of the lowest point in their mutual story.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是他们共同故事中最灰暗的时刻。

sentences.en: They behave so badly to her.
sentences.zh: 他们对她太坏了。

sentences.en: I completely agree with you,
sentences.zh: 我完全同意你的看法，

sentences.en: Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆。

sentences.en: This is up to this point.
sentences.zh: 这是目前为止最糟糕的。

sentences.en: Emma Hamilton,
sentences.zh: 艾玛·汉密尔顿，

sentences.en: I deep down, I am going to confess, and I hope the listeners will not judge me for this.
sentences.zh: 在内心深处，我要坦白，希望听众不要因此评判我。

sentences.en: I find her quite annoying, but this is the one point where I think she's genuinely vicious.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她很烦人，但这是我认为她真正恶毒的一点。

sentences.en: Fanny is a beaten woman.
sentences.zh: 范妮是一个被击垮的女人。

sentences.en: Well, so Nelson,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以纳尔逊，

sentences.en: Nelson has this awful phrase.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊有句很糟糕的话。

sentences.en: It is very easy to find a stick if you are inclined to beat your dog.
sentences.zh: 如果你想打狗，总能找到棍子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, that's hard to defend.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那很难辩解。

sentences.en: And that's very hard to defend.
sentences.zh: 而且那真的很难辩解。

sentences.en: I think now, I think in Nelson's case,
sentences.zh: 我想现在，我想就纳尔逊的情况而言，

sentences.en: I'm not saying this makes him better than Emma, by the way, but I think in Nelson's case, this is clearly driven.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我并不是说这让他比艾玛更好，但我认为就纳尔逊而言，这显然是有驱动力的。

sentences.en: Do you not think by guilt?
sentences.zh: 你不认为是出于内疚吗？

sentences.en: He hates feeling bad about himself.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌对自己感觉不好。

sentences.en: You know, he's been brought up by a vicar in a vicarage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他是在牧师住宅里由一位牧师抚养长大的。

sentences.en: He's been told how to behave and he knows he's letting his father and his moral code down.
sentences.zh: 他被教导过如何行事，他知道自己辜负了父亲和道德准则。

sentences.en: There's a slight sense of viciousness and anger to the way he treats Fanny, because he feels that she has driven him to behave badly and he doesn't like it.
sentences.zh: 他对待范妮的方式中有一种轻微的恶毒和愤怒，因为他觉得是她逼得他行为不端，而他并不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: But what's interesting is he doesn't blame Emma for this.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，他并没有因此责怪艾玛。

sentences.en: I mean, he could easily have done that, but actually it seems to have forced them into an even greater kind of codependency,
sentences.zh: 我是说，他本可以轻易做到这一点，但实际上这似乎迫使他们陷入了一种更深层次的相互依赖，

sentences.en: although it does not in any way inhibit his capacity to feel jealous, as we all see.
sentences.zh: 尽管正如我们所见，这丝毫没有抑制他产生嫉妒的能力。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And now I think one, actually one other aspect, actually,
sentences.zh: 现在我想还有一点，实际上还有另一个方面，

sentences.en: I mean, we could get bogged down in this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们可能会陷入其中。

sentences.en: So one thing that is worth people remembering is Emma and Nelson can move on from this.
sentences.zh: 所以有一件事值得人们记住，那就是艾玛和纳尔逊可以从这件事中走出来。

sentences.en: They can still have the relationship.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然可以维持这段关系。

sentences.en: And the sad thing for Fanny is she can't ever move on and she never, ever does because an abandoned wife can't take on a new partner.
sentences.zh: 而对范妮来说可悲的是，她永远无法走出来，也永远不会走出来，因为被抛弃的妻子无法再找新伴侣。

sentences.en: So she's effectively condemned to live as a kind of widow.
sentences.zh: 所以她实际上注定要像寡妇一样生活。

sentences.en: As I think John Sugden says, an object of pity and innuendo for the remainder of her days.
sentences.zh: 正如我认为约翰·萨格登所说，她余生都将是怜悯和影射的对象。

sentences.en: And that is, that is a really sad story.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个非常悲伤的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, I suppose I'd say the one, the one advantage she has over Emma is that, you know, we talked about Nelson making a financial settlement on her.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我想我会说她比艾玛拥有的一个优势是，你知道，我们谈到过纳尔逊为她做了经济安排。

sentences.en: She will get his pension in due course when he dies.
sentences.zh: 他去世后，她理所当然会得到他的养老金。

sentences.en: You know, she's the one who will receive his prize money and so forth.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她才是那个会收到他的奖金等等的人。

sentences.en: And this, as we will see for Emma is going to be a catastrophe because she, she does lack.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，这对艾玛来说将是一场灾难，因为她确实缺乏这些。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: Emma gets Nelson, but she doesn't get the financial stability that Nelson gives to Fanny.
sentences.zh: 艾玛得到了纳尔逊，但她没有得到纳尔逊给范妮的那种经济保障。

sentences.en: And that's quite a Jane Austen perspective on things.
sentences.zh: 这在简·奥斯汀看来是相当有见地的。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: That's the end of that.
sentences.zh: 那部分就到此为止。

sentences.en: A very sad story.
sentences.zh: 一个非常悲伤的故事。

sentences.en: Let's get back to the action.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到正题。

sentences.en: The 5th of March, after Nelson has written his final sort of letter of dismissal to Fanny, he goes off to Yarmouth, which is on the Norfolk coast on the east of England.
sentences.zh: 3月5日，在纳尔逊写完给范妮的最后一封类似解雇信的信后，他前往雅茅斯，那是在英格兰东部的诺福克海岸。

sentences.en: And there,
sentences.zh: 在那里，

sentences.en: Admiral Hyde Parker's fleet is waiting.
sentences.zh: 海德·帕克海军上将的舰队正在等待。

sentences.en: Nelson cannot wait to get into action, to leave all this emotional drama behind, but in a sort of weird mirror image of what's been going on.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊迫不及待地想投入战斗，把所有这些情感纠葛抛在脑后，但这与正在发生的事情形成了一种奇怪的镜像。

sentences.en: Admiral Parker has an interesting love life of his own.
sentences.zh: 帕克海军上将自己的爱情生活也很有趣。

sentences.en: He's 61 years old.
sentences.zh: 他61岁了。

sentences.en: He's a very kind of cautious, pedantic, meticulous admiral, but he's just married a new bride and her age is variously given at 24.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常谨慎、迂腐、一丝不苟的海军上将，但他刚娶了一位新娘，她的年龄有不同说法，说是24岁。

sentences.en: Remember he's 61 or by some sources as 18.
sentences.zh: 记住他61岁，或者据某些消息来源说是18岁。

sentences.en: There's a bit of a gap.
sentences.zh: 这中间有点差距。

sentences.en: Now,
sentences.zh: 现在，

sentences.en: Admiral Hyde Parker loves, he's delighted.
sentences.zh: 海德·帕克海军上将很爱，他很高兴。

sentences.en: He's having a tremendous time and he's in no hurry to go sailing off to the Baltic when he's got this teenage bride.
sentences.zh: 他过得很愉快，既然有了这位十几岁的新娘，他一点也不急着去波罗的海航行。

sentences.en: So while, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以当，你知道，

sentences.en: Nelson is chafing,
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊感到焦躁不安时，

sentences.en: Admiral Hyde Parker is organizing balls and parties and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 海德·帕克海军上将却在组织舞会、派对之类的活动。

sentences.en: And so they don't set off for another week.
sentences.zh: 所以他们又过了一周才出发。

sentences.en: But Dominic, the thing is that even when they do set off and you'd think that,
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，问题是即使他们出发了，你本以为，

sentences.en: Nelson's focus now would be all about the campaign to come, he's still obsessing about Emma and he's still obsessing about,
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊现在的焦点应该是即将到来的战役，但他仍然沉迷于艾玛，仍然沉迷于，

sentences.en: about the Prince of Wales and kind of writing letters to her all the time.
sentences.zh: 关于威尔士亲王的事，而且一直在给她写信。

sentences.en: And I always think when I read about this campaign and you read all the letters that he's sending to Emma,
sentences.zh: 我每次读到关于这场战役的内容，读到他发给艾玛的所有信件时，我总是觉得，

sentences.en: it's unbelievable that he has the focus and capacity to achieve what he achieves on this campaign.
sentences.zh: 他竟然有专注力和能力在这场战役中取得那样的成就，真是令人难以置信。

sentences.en: I mean, it's astonishing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太惊人了。

sentences.en: Copenhagen is an, is an amazing story, which we'll come to.
sentences.zh: 哥本哈根是一个了不起的故事，我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: The incredible thing is that basically the build up to it, he's writing a letter saying,
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，基本上在准备阶段，他写信说，

sentences.en: Sir William Hamilton's pimping you out.
sentences.zh: 威廉·汉密尔顿爵士在把你当妓女一样推销。

sentences.en: What are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你在做什么？

sentences.en: How are you associating with a set of whores, boards and unprincipled liars, all of this kind of thing?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能和一群妓女、无赖和毫无原则的骗子混在一起，诸如此类？

sentences.en: He writes about his dreams, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他写到了他的梦，不是吗？

sentences.en: He says, there's a dream in which I hit you over there with a stick and then threw a tub of boiling hot water over you because of the Prince.
sentences.zh: 他说，我做了一个梦，梦见因为那个亲王，我用棍子打了你，然后把一桶滚烫的热水泼在你身上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: That's a strange letter to get from your lover.
sentences.zh: 从爱人那里收到这样的信真是奇怪。

sentences.zh: 我想艾玛会顺其自然的。

sentences.en: You reckon?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's the kind of, you know, the kind of the drama of it all, the melodrama.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是那种，你知道，那种戏剧性，那种情节剧。

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, as they sail northeast through the North Sea, the pace of events is quickening.
sentences.zh: 现在，与此同时，当他们向东北穿过北海航行时，事件的节奏正在加快。

sentences.en: On the 14th of March, the Admiralty sends them their final instructions.
sentences.zh: 3月14日，海军部向他们发出了最终指令。

sentences.en: We want you to force the straits between Denmark and Sweden, annihilate the Danish fleet and the dockyards at Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 我们要你们强行通过丹麦和瑞典之间的海峡，歼灭丹麦舰队和哥本哈根的造船厂。

sentences.en: And if this isn't enough to intimidate the other Baltic powers, we want you to head on towards the Russian naval base at Kronstadt and hurry, hurry, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果这还不足以威慑其他波罗的海大国，我们要你们继续前往俄罗斯在喀琅施塔得的海军基地，快点，快点，你知道，

sentences.en: time is of the essence.
sentences.zh: 时间紧迫。
